title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning
abstract: arXiv:2610.31786v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Federated unlearning (FU) aims to remove a designated target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch. Existing methods largely treat unlearning as a post-hoc, stateless operation, overlooking that client influence is path-dependent: contributions made during training, particularly during critical learning periods (CLPs), can have disproportionate and persistent effects. Moreover, knowledge overlap and intermittent client availability make relying on all retained clients inefficient and impractical. We introduce PDF, a path-dependent client-selection framework based on the insight that retained clients are not equally valuable for unlearning. During training, PDF maintains lightweight, target-agnostic, CLP-weighted histories summarizing each client's accumulated update direction and global-model alignment. Upon an unlearning request, these histories identify and rank retained clients

translated_title: 并非所有保留客户端都是平等的：联邦遗忘中的客户端选择
translated_abstract: 联邦遗忘旨在从已训练的模型中移除指定目标客户端的影响，而无需承担从头重新训练的过高成本。现有方法大多将遗忘视为一种事后、无状态的操作，忽略了客户端影响是路径依赖的：训练期间（尤其是在关键学习期间，CLP）所做的贡献可能产生不成比例且持久的影响。此外，知识重叠和客户端的间歇性可用性使得依赖所有保留客户端既低效又不切实际。我们提出了PDF，一个路径依赖的客户端选择框架，其基于这样一个洞察：保留客户端对遗忘任务的价值并不相等。在训练期间，PDF维护轻量级、与目标无关的、经CLP加权的历史记录，总结每个客户端累积的更新方向以及与全局模型的对齐程度。在收到遗忘请求时，这些历史记录会识别并排序保留客户端。
tldr: 提出PDF框架，通过在训练期间维护路径依赖、CLP加权的轻量级客户端历史信息，在联邦遗忘时识别并排序最有价值的保留客户端，而非盲目依赖所有保留客户端，从而更高效地移除目标客户端的影响。
en_tdlr: PDF is a path-dependent client-selection framework for federated unlearning that leverages lightweight, CLP-weighted client histories maintained during training to identify and rank the most valuable retained clients, instead of naively relying on all of them.
